cases.setup: Search input focused with multiple results loaded.
cases.action: Use ArrowDown to enter result navigation, then press Enter outside IME composition.
assert: the selected item and scrolled item agree
one user action creates at most one job
the input caret retains ordinary arrow-key behavior

cases.setup: Search input is in an active IME composition; the panel is visible and a result is selected.
cases.action: Press Escape to cancel composition; in a separate active composition press Enter to confirm; after composition ends, press Enter again.
assert: IME Escape cancels composition without creating a paste job or hiding the panel
composition Enter creates no paste job and does not close the panel
a later non-composing Enter creates exactly one job

cases.setup: A card is idle, then repeat the click/double-click and held/repeated Enter sequences while a job is busy.
cases.action: Observe selected item, job count, and clipboard/input call counts.
assert: a single click preserves the existing select-and-execute behavior
the dblclick handler adds no extra execution
event.repeat and busy state do not create overlapping duplicate jobs

cases.setup: Clipboard sequence is unchanged across repeated notifications or legacy polling ticks.
cases.action: Run clipboard capture for the unchanged sequence.
assert: content read/decode/PNG/Base64/hash counts remain zero after sequence comparison

cases.setup: A new clipboard sequence contains an image; duplicate notifications for that sequence follow.
cases.action: Process the sequence and then select/copy its stored item.
assert: the sequence is captured once
duplicate notifications and selecting the stored image do not repeat PNG/Base64/hash work

cases.setup: The decoded-image cache misses for a valid image.
cases.action: Select it while preparation runs and then let preparation finish.
assert: preparing is observable
the UI remains responsive
the original is retained and is not replaced by a downsampled thumbnail

cases.setup: Drive worker, decoded-cache, image-size, and queue limits to and beyond their configured boundaries.
cases.action: Submit valid and over-budget image work, including cancellation and a permission/read failure.
assert: fake fixtures cover the configured single-worker, 32MiB decoded-cache, and 20MiB/16MP per-image boundaries; 256MiB peak-worker RSS must be measured separately and is not established by fake limits
P07/P08 cancellation, P14 permission degradation, and P17 capacity failures are explicit
failed work does not overwrite clipboard or discard the retained original

cases.setup: An image cache miss starts with a fixed monotonic content-preparation deadline; the fake worker never completes until it receives abort.
cases.action: Allow the 3000ms deadline to expire, then submit a new image after the timed-out worker has been disposed.
assert: the original absolute deadline returns image_prepare_timeout and aborts the worker signal
the timed-out worker is disposed and is not reused for the next decode
timeout leaves no decoded cache entry and never reports ready

cases.setup: A selection starts a continuously polled trigger/modifier-key monitor at time zero alongside content preparation, with the original absolute 500ms key-release cutoff and separate 3000ms content-preparation deadline.
cases.action: Run these fake timelines: held through 500ms then released at 700ms with preparation ending at 800ms; initially released then re-pressed at 400ms through 500ms and released at 700ms with preparation ending at 800ms; released at 490ms with preparation ending at 2500ms.
assert: a key held at the original 500ms cutoff latches key_held; a later release cannot resume the selection
a key re-press observed during preparation is not masked by an earlier released sample
held-at-cutoff cases produce zero clipboard writes, input submissions, and panel hides
release observed before the cutoff permits preparation to finish after 500ms but before 3000ms and continue immediately after a current key-state recheck
when preparation finishes after the released cutoff, main omits the expired helper deadline; a commit that starts before cutoff still carries the original absolute deadline

cases.setup: A timed-out fake worker's dispose promise never resolves.
cases.action: Submit later preparation requests with their own short absolute deadlines.
assert: each request waiting for retirement returns image_prepare_timeout by its own deadline
retirement remains latched and no replacement worker is created

cases.setup: Multiple results are loaded and a non-first item is selected. Choose a new query that returns multiple results and still includes the previously selected item; open/close the panel with reduced motion both enabled and disabled.
cases.action: Change the query, then observe the selected card and viewport; navigate results by keyboard and observe the final window bounds and content transition.
assert: after query change, selection resets to the first result in the new query and that result is visible even when the prior selection still matches
keyboard selection and scrolling stay aligned
one final bounds update is applied
reduced motion disables positional animation

cases.setup: Search query is empty with a large fake item set.
cases.action: Render the initial list and count body-search calls.
assert: empty query does not scan item bodies
the initial visible list remains correct

cases.setup: A selection is canceled while its key-release monitor is polling and preparation has not finished.
cases.action: Cancel the selection and observe the monitor wait and scheduled polling timer.
assert: the pending monitor wait resolves selection_cancelled
the timer is cleared and no clipboard, input, or panel-hide effect occurs

cases.setup: The fake scheduler delays the selection monitor callback until after both absolute 500ms deadlines; the last observed key state is released, then the fake key is re-pressed before 500ms and released after 500ms.
cases.action: Advance the fake clock across the cutoff without running scheduled polls, then complete the selection preparation.
assert: the missed cutoff returns key_state_unavailable instead of trusting the stale released sample
no clipboard write, input submission, or panel hide occurs
this fake scheduler case does not establish behavior under a real main-process event-loop stall

cases.setup: A selection's 500ms key-release monitor reaches its cutoff while image preparation is still pending; test both a held key and a released key.
cases.action: For the held case, abort preparation at 500ms and make its pending promise reject later with image_prepare_timeout. For the released case, let the cutoff settle while preparation remains pending, then finish preparation.
assert: held-at-cutoff returns key_held even when preparation later reports image_prepare_timeout, and invokes cancellation once
the blocked result causes zero clipboard writes, input submissions, and panel hides; no helper registration request is made while snapshot preparation is pending
released-at-cutoff continues waiting for preparation and does not invoke cancellation
both terminal paths clear the monitor timer

cases.setup: The original 500ms key-release cutoff has elapsed with a released-key sample and image preparation completes afterward.
cases.action: Commit through the main/helper contract with a zero selection budget; exercise released keys and a key re-press before the helper clipboard-write gate.
assert: zero budget performs an immediate key-state check and never starts a fresh 500ms wait
released keys permit clipboard commit, while a re-pressed key blocks input submission
a key held at check-only commit blocks clipboard commit
this isolated fake does not establish physical keyboard timing or the OS-level race after the final key sample

Let the real monitor timer resume after the original cutoff; if the production work returns early, use separately reported harness-only blocking to force an overdue timer callback.
assert: The nativeImage PNG output exceeds 20 MiB and the production encoder invokes JPEG quality 82 within the 20 MiB cap.
Record fixture preparation separately from PNG, JPEG, Base64/SHA-256, and any harness-only event-loop stall time.
An overdue poll after both deadline clocks have expired returns key_state_unavailable without treating the pre-stall released sample as current.
